query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a dual-phase structure with stepwise and independently controllable dual coherent precipitation in a eutectic high-entropy alloy can improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase lamellar structure
generation.intervention: Introducing a stepwise and independently controllable dual coherent precipitation structure
generation.conditions: Ambient temperature and multistage thermo-mechanical processing
generation.mechanism: Synergistic effect of dual coherent precipitation on strength and ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength and room-temperature tensile ductility
generation.baseline: Conventional eutectic high-entropy alloy with a single-phase structure
generation.boundary: Limitations of conventional processing methods and single-phase structures
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the optimal composition and processing conditions for achieving the desired dual-phase structure

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of mechanical properties between eutectic high-entropy alloys with single-phase and dual-phase structures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the dual-phase structure does not show improved strength and ductility compared to the single-phase structure, the hypothesis is falsified.
